newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters won't exclude deal with Bolger-led National.
newsitem.headline: Peters won't exclude deal with Bolger-led National.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters on Thursday refused to rule out the possibility of coalition with a National Party led by Jim Bolger.

He said in an interview with Radio New Zealand that the statement that NZ First would only deal with National if it dumped prime minister Bolger, Finance Minister Bill Birch and Health Minister Jenny Shipley was the personal view only of NZ First deputy leader Tau Henare.
"Have you seen me say that? He said it was his personal view," Peters said.

On coalitions, he said NZ First had never deviated from the position taken in April 1994 where it said it would make a decision as a caucus with the best interests of the country's economic and social future in mind.
Peters said it was impossible for NZ First to give an indication of which party it was leaning towards until it had had had detailed discussions with other parties.
"No discussions have taken place, not even an agreement as to holding a discussion," he said.
"To suggest that you were going to take sides without knowing any of the conditions is to suggest that you advise your party to sign up to a blank contract."
"We will go with the party that understands what we started this party for, what our principles and policies are, and gives us the opportunity to implement those policies," Peters said.
"It's true that our social policy is closer to Labour's, but then the Labour Party's economic policy simply won't stack up. It's simply not possible."

Asked about his earlier statement that the buy-back of Forestry Corp was a condition of forming a coalition with any other party, he said: "New Zealand First is not going to be dealing with parties who regard that of no great moment."

"We think the resources of this country should be owned by the people of this country for the employment and wealth-creation and the benefit of this country. That's our stated foundation of principle and we are not going back on it."
Peters reiterated NZ First's position on foreign investment.
"Our position on strategic assets is very clear -- 24.9 percent and that's it, nothing higher than that."
But he said in other areas, NZ First's wanted New Zealand enterprises to have access to New Zealand money.
He said with all banks being foreign owned, New Zealand was a prisoner of foreign money. Long-term, he expects NZ First's planned compulsory pension scheme to rectify the positon.

Asked if he would accept the position of deputy prime minister to Labour's Helen Clark, Peters said: "I would not be looking to take any job no matter how low or how high on the basis of 'well I've got the job', nothing else matters.
"I think what matters is that we have a detailed agreement, incorporating the policies and strategies to ensure that over three years they are implemented. That's what matters."
